Advocate for Petitioner: Sri. G.R.Subba Reddy Advocate for Respondent No.2 : Smt. R. Sharadamba Respondent No.1 : Exparte  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Smt. Sunandamma A.V., caused in a road traffic accident.
2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 30.10.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. the deceased Sunandamma was proceeding in a Motorcycle Suzuki Access bearing Reg.

No.KA-02-HE-8007 as pillion rider from Yeshwanthapura towards Vijaynagara and the deceased brother riding the said motorcycle and when they reached near Rajajinagara Dobighat, West of Chord Service Road, in front of Lakshminarayana Nilaya, at that time, a Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-AG-9219 came from backside and the driver of the said lorry was driven in a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle Suzuki Access from behind.
As a result of which, the motorcycle fell down along with rider and pillion rider and the said lorry ran over the deceased head and the deceased died on the spot
. Thereafter deceased body was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital for Postmortem.

The Post mortem was conducted at M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital and after conducting Post mortem the deceased body was handed over to the family members of the deceased for cremation and spent Rs.3 lakhs towards transportation of body and last rites and rituals of the deceased.
Further stated that due to death of Smt. Sunandamma A.V., the petitioners lost love and affection and earning member of the family.
Hence petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondent.
3. After service of notice to respondents, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that as on the date of the alleged accident the Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AG-9219 was not insured with this respondent.
Further contended that the driver of the lorry was not holding valid driving license to drive said class of vehicle, the same amounts to violation of policy conditions.
The said vehicle is a commercial vehicle and the same was plied on road without there being a valid permit, authorization and Fitness certificate.

Further contended that the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motor cycle and she was not seated properly, further the rider of the motor cycle was proceeding in high speed and suddenly applied break due to said impact, she fell down from the motor cycle.
Hence the entire negligence is on the part of the rider of the motor cycle and also on the part of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is very much excessive, exorbitant, imaginary and baseless.

Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
4.

On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES Shilpa K.V vs Krishnamurthy on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7594820/
2

1. Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased Sunandamma A.V. W/o Late.
Veerabhadrachar C., died due to the grievous injury sustained by her in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No.
KA-02-AG-9219 on 30.10.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. in front of Lakshmi Narayana Nilaya, West of Cord Road, Dhobhigat Junction, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru and she succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioner prove that she is the legal representative of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
5. The Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined another witness as PW.2 and got marked Ex-P1 to 20 documents on behalf of the petitioner.
The respondent has not lead either oral or documentary evidence.
6. Arguments were addressed on both side.
7. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,
petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and eye witness i.e., the rider of motor cycle in which the deceased was travelling as pillion rider as PW.2

and got marked 20 documents as Ex-P1 to Ex-P20 i.e., FIR, complaint, Crime detail form, spot sketc,
IMV report, Inquest report, PM report, Charge sheet, Salary slips, Death certificates,
SSLC marks card, Aadhar cards, Family tree, working letter and Canara bank account statement.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed the objection and seriously disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and also seriously disputed that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

Further respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the lorry was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said clause of vehicle and also did not having the valid Permit, Authorization and Fitness Certificate.

Further, respondent No.2 contended that while the deceased was proceeding as Shilpa K.V vs Krishnamurthy on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7594820/
3 pillion rider in the motorcycle, she was not seated properly and the rider of the motorcycle was proceeding with high speed and suddenly applied break due to said impact, she fell down from the motorcycle and the entire negligence is on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and also on the part of the deceased and hence prays to dismiss the petition.
10.

In the line of arguments, if the material and evidence on record are perused, the accident has been taken place on 30.10.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. and thereafter immediately the rider of the motorcycle Parashiva Murthy lodged the complaint as per Ex.P2 against driver of the BBMP Sewage lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AG-9219 at about 7.30 p.m.

Based on complaint, the jurisdictional police have registered the FIR as per Ex.P1 and conducted thorough and detailed investigation and have filed the charge sheet against driver of the BBMP Sewage lorry by name Marappa S/o.

Narayanappa by holding that on 30.10.2020 at about 6.15 p.m. the accused drove BBMP Garbage disposal compactor bearing Reg. No.KA-02-AG-9219 on the service road of Westcard road,
Rajajinagar, near Wariyar Bekary Junction, in front of house No.1967 from Yashwanthpura towards Vijayanagar, with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the hind portion of the Suzuki Axis Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HE-8007 which was proceeding in the same road and in a same direction.
Due to the impact, the rider Parashiva Murthy along with the pillion rider Sunandamma fell down along with the scooter.
Parashiva Murthy fell down on the left side of the road and the Sunandamma pillion rider fell on the right side of the road and the driver of the lorry ran over the head and face of the Sunandamma.
Due to which, Sunandamma sustained crush and grievous blood injuries, due to which, succumbed at the spot.
Even Parashiva Murthy has sustained simple injuries of his both hands and left knee.

Accordingly, the investigating officer has submitted charge sheet against the driver of the Lorry for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(a)
of IPC.
11.

The respondent No.2 though in his written statement disputed the involvement of the vehicle and cause of the accident, but, respondents have not led any evidence and produce any material on record to prove their contention and even no material and evidence brought on record to prove the charge sheet filed by the investigating officer is defective and collusive.

12. The PW.2 who is an eye witness and material witness in his evidence clearly deposed about the cause and manner of the accident and also about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry and due to which, the driver of the lorry hit to the hind portion of their motorcycle, as a result,
the Sunandamma pillion rider fell on the right side of the road and lorry ran over her sister head and died on the spot.
13. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 cross examined PW.2 at length, but, not at all denied the cause and manner of accident deposed by the PW.2 atleast by way of putting a single suggestion.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 only posed the bare suggestion that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of PW.2 which was out rightly denied by the PW.2.
Even nothing was brought on record to disprove the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 in the cross-examination.

Shilpa K.V vs Krishnamurthy on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7594820/
4 14.
Apart from this, on perusal of the spot mahazar Ex.P3 and spot sketch Ex.P4, it is clear that the accident has been taken place in the service road of Westcard road.
Further Ex.P4 clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry.
Ex.P4 clearly shows that the PW.2 was riding the motorcycle] on left side of the road and the lorry was driving on right side of the bike.
Further it is clearly shows that, the driver of the Lorry has hit to the hind portion of the motorcycle.
The very manner of the accident clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry.
Even respondents have not examined the driver of the lorry to disprove the evidence of the petitioner and PW.2 and to prove their contention.
All these documents clearly shows that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
Moreover all these documents have not at all been disputed by the respondents.

15. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
16. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
17. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

18. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUES NO.2 :
The petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the daughter of deceased Sunandamma.
The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P13 to 15-Aadhaar cards and Ex-P16- Family Tree reveals that the petitioner is the daughter of deceased.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
20. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

In the Ex-P13-Aadhar card, it reveals that date of birth of Smt. Sunandamma is 01.07.1963 and accident has been taken place on Shilpa K.V vs Krishnamurthy on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7594820/
5 30.10.2020 which indicates that she was aged 57 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 i.e., as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '9'.
21. PW-1 contended that deceased Smt. Sunandamma was working as Tailor and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.
In this regard, PW-1 has produced Bank statement as per Ex.P20 and produced Ex-P9 salary certificates which reveals that deceased was getting salary of Rs.11,657/-p.m.

But petitioner has not adduced the evidence who has issued the Ex-P9.
22.
As the accident took place in the year 2020 and since the deceased was a Tailor, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,500/- p.m.

Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.
23.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case, towards her future prospectus if 10% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.15,950/- (14,500 + 1,450).
The deceased was married and having one dependent.
Hence 1/2th of her income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2th of Rs.15,950/- works out to Rs.7,975/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.7,975/- (15,950 - 7,975).
Annual income works out to Rs.95,700/- (7,975 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '9'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.8,61,300/- (95,700 X 9).
24. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited V/
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of filial consortium and loss of love & affection.
25. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
26. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

27. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : Rs.8,61,300/-
2 Loss of Consortium : Rs.48,400/-
3 Loss of Estate : Rs.18,150/-

Shilpa K.V vs Krishnamurthy on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7594820/
6 4

Funeral Expenses : Rs.18,150/-
Total Rs.9,46,000/-
Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.9,46,000=00.
27. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

28. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 is insurer is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.4 :
The petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.9,46,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the share amount of Petitioner a sum 40% shall be deposited in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
